audience.text: Developers building .NET services, desktop tools, or CLI utilities that require deterministic, dependency-free parsing, creation, and inspection of email message formats.

capabilities.text: Load MSG files from streams or files using MapiMessage.FromStream or FromFile, and save messages with Save methods.
capabilities.title: Read and write MSG files

capabilities.text: Build new messages with MapiMessage.Create, set sender and recipient details, and attach files or embedded messages.
capabilities.title: Create messages programmatically

capabilities.text: Parse EML files into MapiMessage objects with LoadFromEml and serialize messages back to MIME with SaveToEml.
capabilities.title: Convert between MSG and EML

capabilities.text: Traverse CFB structure using CfbReader to access sector size, directory entries, and tree-structured content.
capabilities.title: Inspect CFB containers

capabilities.text: Set and retrieve arbitrary MAPI properties via SetProperty and GetPropertyValue beyond strongly-typed members.
capabilities.title: Access MAPI properties

capabilities.text: Add recipients with AddRecipient and attachments with AddAttachment, including embedded messages.
capabilities.title: Attach recipients and files

capabilities.text: Inspect ValidationIssues on loaded messages to detect structural anomalies during parsing.
capabilities.title: Validate message structure

capabilities.text: Construct CFB documents in memory using CfbDocument, CfbStorage, and CfbStream, then serialize with CfbWriter.
capabilities.title: Build CFB containers

limitations.text: No IMAP, SMTP, or POP3 support — the library processes local files only and does not connect to mail servers.
No TNEF support — Transport Neutral Encapsulation Format (winmail.dat) is not parsed or generated.
No dedicated calendar or appointment API — calendar-specific MAPI properties can be accessed generically via SetProperty/GetPropertyValue.
Requires .NET 8.0 or later; classic .NET Framework (4.x) is not supported.

problems_solved.text: Enables reading, writing, and converting MSG and EML formats natively in .NET without requiring Microsoft Outlook or third-party dependencies.
Provides low-level access to CFB container structure for forensic inspection or repair of malformed MSG files.
Supports high-level message manipulation with mutable objects for subject, body, recipients, and attachments.
Performs EML-to-MSG and MSG-to-EML conversion using a native MIME parser without external libraries.

product_summary.text: Aspose.Email FOSS for .NET is a free, open-source .NET library for processing Outlook MSG files, Compound File Binary (CFB) containers, and EML messages without external dependencies or Microsoft Outlook.

uncertainties: The exact scope of 'forensic inspection' capabilities beyond CfbReader and MsgReader is not detailed beyond examples.
Whether MapiMessage.SaveToEml preserves all MIME headers and structure is not explicitly stated.
The behavior of strict parsing mode in MsgReader and MapiMessage is not defined beyond ValidationIssues.
Support for Unicode vs ANSI string handling in MapiMessage.Create is mentioned but not elaborated.
The maximum size or complexity of CFB documents that can be built is not specified.
Whether embedded message attachments support nested CFB structures is not detailed.
The library's handling of non-standard or corrupted MSG files beyond ValidationIssues is not described.
The exact set of supported recipient types in AddRecipient is not listed.

workflows.name: Read MSG file subject
workflows.text: Open an MSG file stream and load it with MapiMessage.FromStream to access message properties like Subject.

workflows.name: Create and save MSG message
workflows.text: Use MapiMessage.Create to build a message in memory, set sender and recipient details, add attachments, and save to disk.

workflows.name: Convert EML to MSG
workflows.text: Load an EML file with MapiMessage.LoadFromEml and persist it as MSG using Save, then regenerate EML with SaveToEml.

workflows.name: Inspect CFB structure
workflows.text: Use CfbReader.FromFile to open a MSG file and traverse its directory tree with IterTree to examine internal layout.
